sections.html:
One department runs the whole system from 135 E. Water Street in Statesville. It has three divisions: assessor, tax collector and land records mapping. The commissioners set policy, but you deal with staff for almost everything.

The office opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 5 p.m. on weekdays. The assessor answers at 704-878-3017 and the collector at 704-878-3020. Mail goes to PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687. More is on the county's Tax Administration page.

  • Assessor division: listing, values, exemptions and appeals.
  • Tax collector division: bills, payments, delinquent accounts and closing payoffs.
  • Land records mapping: parcel maps and the online GIS used to find an owner of record.

A bill question goes to the collector, and a value that looks off goes to the assessor.

Housing here is busy. Mid-2025 population was 211,798 across about 93,711 housing units. The midpoint owned home is $321,400, owners occupy 71.9 percent of occupied homes, and builders took out 1,835 permits in 2025.

The county charges 0.50 per $100 of assessed value for 2026, matching 2025 and 2024, and the 2026-2027 budget keeps it there.

Inside a town, a municipal rate is added, along with any fire or special district. The 2026 figures below come from the county's rate chart, all per $100 of value.

Downtown districts in Statesville (.10) and Mooresville (.14) add to the bill for properties inside them.

The county also bills a flat solid waste fee of $64 per household, mobile home or apartment for 2026, and half of that for an owner with the elderly or disabled exclusion. Davidson adds a $20 privilege charge on vehicles, and Mooresville has its own solid waste fee.

Iredell mails statements in August. Payment is due September 1, and the collector adds nothing before January 5. On January 6 a 2 percent charge applies, and 0.75 percent more joins it each later month.

The statute on due dates and interest explains the January 6 trigger. Some towns and counties offer a discount for paying early. The collector can say if yours does.

Unpaid real estate taxes are advertised in the newspaper each March, with an advertising fee added to the bill. On a delinquent account the collector may use:

  • Attachment of bank accounts
  • Debt set-off against state income tax refunds
  • Garnishment of wages or rents
  • Levy on rents or other money owed to you
  • Seizure of a vehicle or other personal assets
  • Foreclosure

Vehicle tax is a separate matter. It comes with the state tag renewal notice, and you pay it to the DMV rather than the county.

A four-year cycle puts Iredell at double the state's pace, since the minimum is eight. Values last reset January 1, 2023 and reset again January 1, 2027, and the 2027 schedule of values is on the assessor pages. G.S. 105-286 is the outer limit, and a shorter cycle is the county's choice.

Neighborhood by neighborhood, appraisers study recent sales and bring values in line with the market. Sales that are not true market deals get set aside: family transfers, gifts, trades, and forced sales that drag a price down.

The figure on your notice is what bills are based on until the next reappraisal. Listing near a revaluation date? Look up the new appraisal card on the county taxweb site before settling on an asking price.

The process has three steps, taken in order, laid out on the county's appeals page.

  1. Informal review: mail the appeal form and documents to the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, or use the online portal. You have 30 days from the notice date. An appraiser replies with a new notice that may lower, raise or keep the value.
  2. Review board: write out the request, naming the property and your grounds, with a signature from the owner or an attorney. Plan to mail it, and check the method with the assessor at 704-878-3017. The board opens its session in the spring window set by G.S. 105-322.
  3. State commission: still unhappy with the board's written decision? File with the Property Tax Commission within 30 days.

Anyone filing for you who is not an owner or lawyer, such as a friend or tax consultant, must attach a power of attorney or risk rejection. The county's appraisal is presumed correct at the hearing, so you carry the proof. The county wants sales contracts, MLS data or private appraisals dated 2022, plus photos of damage and surveys.

  • Accepted reasons: value out of line with market on the reappraisal date, similar properties assessed differently, or errors on the record card.
  • Rejected reasons: a big increase, inability to pay, weak county services, high taxes, or a market shift after the effective date.

A permanent residence can qualify for one of three state programs. Apply to the assessor on form AV-9.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: owners 65 or older, or totally and lastingly disabled, with 2026 income under $38,800 can exclude $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is larger.
  • Veteran exclusion: $45,000 of value comes off for a permanent, total, service-connected disability, regardless of age or income.
  • Circuit breaker: after five years in the home, tax is capped at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for incomes up to $58,200.

The filing window runs through June 1 ahead of the tax year, as the AV-9 notice shows. The circuit breaker defers the savings under a lien, and selling or moving out triggers repayment of the prior three years. If you are in it, get a payoff from the assessor before listing. Iredell also halves its solid waste fee for owners who hold the elderly exemption.

The same division handles present-use value for farm and forest owners and inventory relief for builders.

sections.h2: Selling and who owes the tax
sections.html:
Ownership is fixed on January 1, so a seller who closes later still owes that year's bill. Splitting it with the buyer is a private deal made at closing.

The collector's position is simple: a transfer does not release the seller, the transfer year's bill goes to the seller, and proration is a matter of contract. Your realtor or closing attorney can explain how it was split. Asking for payment to the collector at closing ties up loose ends, and the office accepts a prepayment at last year's rate when the new bill is not yet out.

Back taxes are the bigger danger. Under G.S. 105-355 a lien reaches the parcel on the listing date, which is why a buyer's lawyer wants the account current. The county names the owner of record at the delinquency date in its advertisement, so get a payoff figure before signing a contract.

A quick cash closing follows the same steps. Call the collector at 704-878-3020 for the payoff and have the closing attorney pay it from your proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the Iredell County property tax rate?
faqs.a: For 2026 it is .50 per $100, with Statesville, Mooresville and other towns adding theirs. Look up your town and fire district on the county rates page.

faqs.q: When must Iredell County taxes be paid?
faqs.a: September 1 is the due date, with nothing added through January 5. After that, 2 percent applies, and then 0.75 percent more monthly.

faqs.q: Where do I file an appeal?
faqs.a: Begin with the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, inside 30 days of your notice. A written appeal to the county review board comes next, then the state Property Tax Commission.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when I sell?
faqs.a: If you sell after January 1, the bill for that year stays yours. Any split with the buyer comes from the contract or closing, and you may ask to pay the collector at closing.

faqs.q: Does Iredell County offer relief for older homeowners?
faqs.a: Yes. The elderly or disabled exclusion is open to owners 65 and older, or disabled, within the income limit, with applications through June 1. Those owners also pay half the solid waste fee.
